Testimony of Senator James Libby
Sponsor of LD 200, "Resolve to Rename the Sebego Lake Crossing Bridge in the Town of
Standish"
Tuesday, February 27, 2025
State House, Room 126, 9:00am

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and the esteemed members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation.
My name is Jim Libby, and I am a State Senator representing Senate District # 22, comprised of
the towns of Naples, Sebago, Baldwin, and Standish in Cumberland County; Hiram and Porter in Oxford County; and, Limington, Limerick, Cornish, Parsonsfield, Newfield, Acton, and Shapleigh, in the County of York.
It is my honor to bring to your attention the contents of L.D. 200, "Resolve to Rename the Sebego Lake Crossing Bridge in the Town of Standish."
This bill seeks to honor those who have served in our armed forces by renaming this bridge the Town of Standish Veterans Memorial Bridge.
I have the approval from the town of Standish for this renaming. I join the town of Standish in
"Recognizing the bravery and sacrifices of our veterans, who have protected our freedom, by
having this bridge renamed to honor them." 1

I hope you join me in recognizing the brave men and woman who fought to protect our country

by renaming this bridge after them.

Testimony of Meghan Russo Maine Department of Transportation
Before the 132"" Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Neither For Nor Against
LD 200, Resolve, T0 Rename the Sebago Lake Road Crossing Bridge in the Town of
Standish
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at
MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 200.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we are not aware of any previous legislatively-sanctioned names for this bridge. MaineDOT's
current inventory number for this structure is 3907.
Thank you.
